_readme: Per-strip FILING corrections, applied by `npm run ingest-frames` after the
strip is cut. This is not a place to touch art: it is for defects that are
mechanical to state and mechanical to undo, so that the correction survives
a --reingest instead of being a hand-edit of an SVG that the next run wipes.
mirrorFrames  1-based frame numbers to flip horizontally, for when one
frame of a strip was drawn facing the opposite way to its
siblings. Only valid because these are side-on figures of
symmetric movements — a flip changes which limb is near,
nothing else. If a movement is genuinely one-sided, the
Every entry needs a `why` with the date. An entry whose strip gets
regenerated should be deleted in the same change.

urdhva-dhanurasana--m.why: 2026-09-04 (Sal, Wheel Pose): frame 1 faces left while frame 2 — and the whole of urdhva-dhanurasana--f — faces right.

vyaghrasana--f.why: 2026-09-04 (Sal, Tiger Pose): frame 1 faces left while frame 2 — and both frames of vyaghrasana--m — face right.

karnapidasana--m.why: 2026-09-04 (Sal, Ear-Pressing Pose): frame 1 lies head-left while frame 2 lies head-right; verified by flipping frame 1 and matching it against frame 2.

sirsasana--f.why: 2026-09-04 (Sal, Headstand): frame 1 tucks to the left while frame 2 — and both frames of sirsasana--m — put the head-and-forearms base on the left with the body to the right.

thoracic-rotation--m.why: 2026-09-04: frame 1 faces left, frames 2-3 face right (found by the corpus-wide facing sweep, not reported by Sal).

ardha-chandrasana--f.why: 2026-09-04: frame 2 faces left while frame 1 and both frames of ardha-chandrasana--m face right.

dragon-flag--m.why: 2026-09-04 (Sal): frame 2 was drawn facing the opposite way to frames 1 and 3 — the figure flips end-for-end mid-movement.

decline-dumbbell-press--f.why: 2026-09-04 (Sal): frame 1 (head right, bench declining left) is mirrored relative to frames 2-3.

inverted-row--m.why: 2026-09-04 (Sal): frame 3 was drawn facing left while frames 1-2 face right, so the figure appeared to spin round mid-movement.
